key: And it was so from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel unto this day.
s: After the rout of the Amalekite raiders, David rules that the two hundred men left behind at the brook share the spoil with those who fought; Rashi, on 30:25, reads the Hebrew wording as reaching back in time, since Abraham had already set this rule.

evidence.words: לא נאמר והלאה, אלא ומעלה, כבר הנהיג אברהם בחוק זה (בראשית יד כד): 'בלעדי רק אשר אכלו הנערים' וגו', הם היושבים על הכלים, 'וחלק האנשים', ההולכים במלחמה
evidence.gloss: It does not say ‘onward’ but ‘and upward’ [that is, before]: Abraham had already set this statute (Genesis 14:24), ‘save only that which the young men have eaten’, those who sat by the baggage, ‘and the portion of the men’, those who went to war.

reason: Second judgement: the refuter is right. The earlier plain sense said ‘the men who guarded the baggage’, but day.js has the two hundred who were too faint to cross the brook Besor and were made to abide there (30:10, 30:21) and, at 30:24, him ‘that tarrieth by the baggage’; guarding is Metzudat David’s reason on 30:24, not the text. Changed only the context clause to ‘the two hundred men left behind at the brook’. The reading stands: Rashi on 30:25 (packet, Hebrew On Your Way) says the verse says ומעלה not והלאה because Abraham had already set this statute (Genesis 14:24), citing Genesis Rabbah 43:9, which he adopts. Radak has nothing on 30:25; Metzudat David reads it forward (for all time until the exile), not a contrary reading. verse.js ok, ref 1 Samuel 30:25 at [261,25]; entry-check ok on scratch/RV-d096-p.json.
